findings.checklist_item: Specify that a criterion which cannot produce at least one expect:finding AND at least one expect:pass candidate is skipped (emits no spec), so every emitted file necessarily satisfies the eval.py:252-255 balance rule.
evidence: 'Per criterion at most 8 cases, targeting 4 expect: finding and 4 expect: pass, satisfying the balance rule at eval.py:252-255'
eval.py:255 emits 'strict: dataset must be balanced (>=1 should-fire AND >=1 pass case)' when only one side is present
AC4: 'Every emitted spec passes validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True) with zero returned errors'
findings.finding: The 'Emitted shape' only says it TARGETS 4 expect:finding and 4 expect:pass to satisfy the eval.py:252-255 balance rule, but the mechanism provides no guarantee a given criterion yields at least one of each. must-not-fire candidates come solely from negative reproduction consensus, which can be empty for a criterion that never went silent on repeated material; conversely a criterion may yield only pass candidates. In either case the emitted spec would carry a fire-only-or-pass-only dataset that FAILS validate_eval_spec(strict=True)'s balance check, contradicting AC4.
scenarios: A criterion mines 3 fire candidates and 0 pass candidates; the miner writes a spec whose only expects are fire, which then fails strict validation — either crashing the run or emitting an invalid file.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Emitted shape: 'A criterion that yields zero candidates on either side of the fire/pass axis is skipped entirely (no file emitted), guaranteeing every written spec satisfies the balance rule; the per-criterion count print records it as skipped-unbalanced.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion asserting that a corpus ticket which passed review then took a plan_defect close (or inbound caused_by link) yields a must-fire (expect: finding) candidate.
evidence: Approach lists 'Escaped defect, used positively only — a ticket that passed review and then took a plan_defect close or an inbound caused_by link (labels.py:70-73) yields a must-fire candidate.'

No acceptance criterion mentions escaped defect, plan_defect close, or caused_by link — the AC list covers vintage, clean_close, blocking conjuncts, validator, skip list, determinism, network guard only.
findings.finding: The 'escaped defect, used positively' must-fire signal is described in Approach but no acceptance criterion verifies it produces a must-fire candidate; every other signal (reproduction consensus, author response, clean_close exclusion, blocking conjuncts) has a covering AC.
findings.location: Approach > Signals ('Escaped defect, used positively only'); Acceptance Criteria list
scenarios: The escaped-defect path silently regresses or is never implemented, and no test catches it because no AC exercises it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'A ticket that passed review and later took a plan_defect close produces an expect: finding candidate for that criterion; verified by pytest over a synthetic escaped-defect row.'

findings.checklist_item: Specify the vintage-gate fallback when a criterion's rubric file (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<C>.md) is absent or its origin/main git-log is empty (e.g. skip project.<name> criteria, or treat a missing boundary as ineligible), and add an AC covering it.
evidence: Plan: 'A review is eligible for criterion C only when its review_event_ts ... postdates the last origin/main commit touching src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<C>.md.'

criteria/overlay.py:354-360 merges project.<name>-prefixed ids into the routing map (merged[cid] = entry); effective_routing therefore can report ids with no plan_review_<name>.md file — the reviewers/ dir ships only built-in rubrics.
The vintage gate has no defined branch for 'rubric file for C does not exist' / 'git-log returns empty': admit-all, skip-all, or error is unspecified.
findings.finding: The vintage gate is specified only as 'the last origin/main commit touching src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<C>.md', but the Scope covers every criterion effective_routing reports, which includes project.<name>-prefixed overlay criteria that have no plan_review_<C>.md rubric file — leaving the gate's behavior undefined (unspecified fallback) when that file is absent or the git-log returns no commit.
findings.location: Approach → 'Vintage gate'; Scope ('criteria that effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review') reports')
scenarios: A repo activates a project.<name> plan_review criterion via the criteria overlay; the miner reaches it because effective_routing lists it, then computes a vintage boundary against a nonexistent plan_review_project.<name>.md.
A built-in criterion whose rubric was renamed/moved so no committed path matches plan_review_<C>.md.
findings.suggested_fix: State that a criterion with no committed src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<C>.md (including project.<name> overlay criteria) fails the vintage gate and is skipped, and add an acceptance criterion asserting a project-prefixed / missing-rubric criterion yields zero candidates.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the vintage-gate result when no `origin/main` commit is found for a criterion's rubric file (or the git query errors) — e.g. treat as no-eligible-reviews and surface it in the per-criterion count rather than defaulting to admit-all.
evidence: 'postdates the last `origin/main` commit touching `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<C>.md`' — no stated behavior when no such commit exists or the git query returns empty/errors
ABSENCE: the git-metadata read is a new failure point but its empty/error result is not surfaced or dispositioned
findings.finding: The vintage gate keys on 'the last `origin/main` commit touching `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_<C>.md`', but the plan does not state the gate's disposition when that lookup yields no commit (a brand-new criterion whose rubric file has no committed history, or a `git log` failure) — the gate could then admit-all, exclude-all, or crash, changing which candidates are mined.
findings.location: Approach — 'Vintage gate. A review is eligible for criterion C only when its `review_event_ts` ... postdates the last `origin/main` commit touching ...'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the miner's behavior when a criterion yields no valid fire or no-fire candidates (e.g. 'a criterion that cannot satisfy the balance rule or a non-empty gold_set emits no spec and is reported in the per-criterion count as 0').
evidence: Emitted shape: 'Per criterion at most 8 cases, targeting 4 expect: finding and 4 expect: pass, satisfying the balance rule at eval.py:252-255, plus a non-empty gold_set.'

must-not-fire candidates come only from 'reproduction consensus in the negative direction' — a criterion with no negative reproduction consensus can produce zero expect: pass cases, which would violate validate_eval_spec(strict=True).
No scope bullet or AC states the termination behavior when a criterion cannot satisfy the balance / gold_set requirement.
findings.finding: The plan requires every emitted spec to carry at least one expect: finding, at least one expect: pass, and a non-empty gold_set (AC4), but does not state what the miner does for a criterion whose signals yield zero fire candidates or zero no-fire candidates — leaving the executor to guess whether such a criterion is skipped, errors, or emits an invalid spec.
scenarios: A criterion has fire candidates but no negative-consensus no-fire candidates; the miner cannot produce a spec passing strict validation.
AC4 says 'every emitted spec passes validate_eval_spec strict' — an under-populated criterion forces either an invalid emission or a silent skip the plan never names.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scope bullet: 'A criterion that cannot produce at least one expect: finding, one expect: pass, and a non-empty gold_set emits no file and is reported with a zero candidate count.'

findings.checklist_item: State explicitly that expect:pass (must-not-fire) candidates are always ADVISORY (never BLOCKING), since the margin and author-response conjuncts are structurally fire-only.
evidence: 'A candidate is proposed BLOCKING only when all four hold: reproduction consensus, author-response corroboration for a fire case, abs(decision_margin) ... at or above ... MIN_MARGIN, and the vintage gate.'
sidecar.py:344 `_decision_margin(finding)` — margin is a per-finding value; a no-fire observation has no finding and no margin
labels.py:158-171 classify_finding_survival labels only findings present in review_k — no analog for a silent criterion
findings.finding: The BLOCKING admission bar names 'author-response corroboration for a fire case' and 'abs(decision_margin) >= MIN_MARGIN' as required conjuncts, but both signals are structurally fire-only: finding_survival is a per-finding label (labels.py:158-171) and decision_margin is computed per-finding as priority-block_threshold (sidecar.py:344-360). A must-not-fire (expect:pass) candidate is a criterion SILENCE with no finding and therefore no margin and no author-response, so no pass candidate can ever satisfy the blocking bar. The plan does not state that pass candidates are always advisory, leaving the tier logic for the pass branch under-specified.
scenarios: A must-not-fire candidate with strong negative reproduction consensus and a wide safety margin can never be admitted as blocking, only advisory, even when it is the most reliable oracle available.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the Tiered admission bar: 'The margin and author-response conjuncts apply only to fire candidates; a must-not-fire candidate reaches at most ADVISORY, on reproduction consensus plus the vintage gate.'

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the working-directory lifecycle: whether each run clears/overwrites the output tree (so stale candidates from a prior run cannot survive) and who retires it, making the byte-identical-across-runs guarantee well-defined.
evidence: 'It writes nothing into `.rebar/evals/` ... so it can be re-run freely'

'Two consecutive real runs over the committed corpus emit byte-identical output' — byte-identical output presumes overwrite/replace semantics, but the plan never states the run clears prior contents; an append or a stale file from a prior criterion set would silently break the byte-identical guarantee and hand the sibling runner obsolete candidates
ABSENCE: no CREATE/RETIRE statement for the working directory shared between miner and admission runner
findings.finding: The working-directory artifact handed to the sibling admission runner has no defined lifecycle: the plan says the miner 'writes CANDIDATE fixture specs to a working directory' and can be 're-run freely' emitting 'byte-identical output', but never states the overwrite/cleanup semantics of that directory on re-run (overwrite vs. append vs. accumulate) or who retires stale candidates when a criterion drops out of the candidate set on a later run.
findings.location: Approach — 'An offline miner that emits CANDIDATE fixture specs to a working directory'; Acceptance Criteria — 'Two consecutive real runs ... emit byte-identical output'
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that each run rebuilds the output directory from empty (or writes to a fresh temp tree then atomically replaces), so no stale per-criterion file survives a criterion becoming skipped/specced.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the miner→admission-runner CANDIDATE contract, the advisory/blocking tier rules, and the MIN_MARGIN rationale in an ADR or design-doc/AGENTS.md update.
evidence: Scope: 'A new module under src/rebar/llm/evals/ holding the miner and its selection predicates.'
Approach describes a new candidate/ADVISORY/BLOCKING tier contract consumed by an unnamed 'sibling admission runner' with no documentation deliverable.
Definition of Done and Acceptance Criteria mention no ADR, AGENTS.md, or design-doc update for the new pipeline stage or its emitted-candidate contract.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new offline candidate-mining pipeline stage feeding a sibling admission runner, with a new signal taxonomy and a MIN_MARGIN tuning knob, but no ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update captures this new pattern or the miner→admission-runner contract.
findings.location: Approach; Scope ('A new module under src/rebar/llm/evals/')
scenarios: A future contributor to the sibling admission runner has no documented spec of the CANDIDATE shape, the tier semantics, or the MIN_MARGIN rationale.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Situate the signal-combination/tiering design against established weak-supervision label mining (e.g. Snorkel-style labeling functions + denoising) and eval-dataset-from-production-logs practice, justifying the hand-rolled conjunction over a standard label model.
evidence: Plan proposes three independent offline signals ('Reproduction consensus', 'Author response', 'Escaped defect') combined into tiered candidates with a MIN_MARGIN noise-floor filter -- structurally identical to weak-supervision labeling functions + denoising
Retrieved: Snorkel AI 'Essential Guide to Weak Supervision' (snorkel.ai/data-centric-ai/weak-supervision) -- combining multiple noisy heuristic label sources via label-model algorithms

Retrieved: 'Language Models in the Loop: Incorporating Prompting into Weak Supervision' (ACM/IMS J. Data Science, dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3617130) -- treating queries as labeling functions denoised with Snorkel

Retrieved: 'How to Build an LLM Eval Dataset from Production Logs' (mljourney.com) and 'Automated Eval Dataset Generator from Production Logs' (github.com/Anas-Amiar/eval-dataset-generator) -- mining production logs into labeled eval cases with stratified sampling, confidence-based routing, and dedup against the existing dataset
findings.finding: The plan's selection methodology (independent noisy signals combined and denoised, a margin/noise-floor filter to drop flaky candidates, tiered blocking/advisory routing, dedup against existing specs) is an instance of well-established external prior art -- weak-supervision label mining (Snorkel-style labeling functions with noise denoising) and building LLM eval datasets from production logs -- but the plan presents it from first principles with no prior-art consideration.
scenarios: A reviewer or maintainer asks why the tier/margin/consensus scheme was designed as-is and whether a standard weak-supervision label model was considered instead of a hand-rolled conjunction
The noise-floor / consensus rules are re-tuned later without reference to established label-denoising practice
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short prior-art note to the Approach section citing weak-supervision label mining (Snorkel) and eval-dataset-from-logs pipelines, and state why a hand-coded conjunction of independent signals with a margin floor is preferred here (small criterion count, need for deterministic/auditable rules, no training step) over a learned label model.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly cite the existing plan_replay tier stack (tier0/1/2, sampling.stratified_sample, candidates, verifier_candidates) as adjacent prior art and state which pieces the miner reuses vs. why fixture emission is a distinct axis.
evidence: Plan states scope is 'A new module under src/rebar/llm/evals/ ... consuming plan_replay/corpus.py and plan_replay/labels.py' but names none of the sibling tier modules
src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/sampling.py already implements deterministic stratified_sample over corpus rows (sampling.py:49)

src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier0.py, tier1.py, tier2.py, candidates/, and verifier_candidates.py already mine/replay the same corpus on adjacent axes (their docstrings explicitly draw axis boundaries -- e.g. tier2.py:1-31, candidates/__init__.py:1-9)
findings.finding: The plan does not acknowledge the repository's existing plan_replay tier infrastructure (tier0/tier1/tier2, sampling.stratified_sample, candidates/, verifier_candidates, labels) as prior art, nor explain why the new miner does not reuse sampling.stratified_sample for its candidate selection, even though that module already extracts stratified signal from the same corpus.
scenarios: A maintainer reviewing the new module asks whether its candidate-selection sampling duplicates sampling.stratified_sample
Future work needs to reconcile the new miner's determinism guarantees with the existing seed-based stratified sampler
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, add one sentence naming sampling.stratified_sample and the tier modules, stating that fixture emission is a distinct axis from decision-math/prompt replay and either reusing stratified_sample for candidate ordering or explaining why a different selection is needed.
